name: Arizona
agency: Arizona Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Division (ADOT MVD)

exam.languages: English, Spanish, Mandarin and others; touchscreen with audio assist (azdot.gov/node/11686, checked 2026-10-09)

permitAge: 15 years and 6 months for a graduated (Class G) instruction permit; 18 for an operator (Class D) permit; valid 12 months (manual p. 10). A restricted instruction permit for students in an approved driver training program is in ARS 28-3153/28-3155, not in the manual.

teen.supervisedHours: 30 hours, at least 10 at night, certified in writing by a parent or guardian; or 20 hours (6 at night) after Traffic Survival School or a Defensive Driving course; or an MVD-approved driver education program instead (manual p. 11)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months; the permit must still be valid when applying for the graduated license (manual p. 11). Class G from 16 to under 18.
teen.nightLimit: First 6 months of the graduated license: no driving midnight to 5 a.m. unless a licensed parent or legal guardian is in the front passenger seat, or driving directly to or from a sanctioned school activity, work, a sanctioned religious activity or a family emergency (manual p. 11).
teen.passengerLimit: First 6 months: no more than one passenger under 18, unless the passengers are siblings or a licensed parent or legal guardian is in the front passenger seat (manual p. 11).
teen.phone: All drivers: may not hold or support a wireless device; no texting or video; hands-free and voice-to-text allowed; handheld only to report an emergency (manual p. 20). Permit holders and the first 6 months of a Class G license: no wireless device at all except in an emergency (ARS 28-3154(C), 28-3174(F); not in the manual).

bac.under21: any amount (zero tolerance; manual p. 47, p. 52)

notes: Knowledge test stops automatically once 80 percent are correct or the maximum misses are reached; retake on the next business day (ADOT).
Move over law (ARS 28-775): applies to any stationary vehicle with flashing lights since 2011; move to a non-adjacent lane if safe, otherwise slow down.

Prima facie speeds (ARS 28-701): 15 mph approaching a school crossing, 25 mph in business or residential districts, 65 mph elsewhere. Rural interstate 75 mph only where ADOT orders it (ARS 28-702.04); not used as a question.
Extreme DUI at 0.15 BAC or more.
8 or more points in 12 months: Traffic Survival School or suspension (ADOT). TSS is required after DUI, wrong-way, red-light or stop-sign, or aggressive driving convictions.
School bus rule on divided highways: Arizona statute text (ARS 28-857) could not be retrieved; no question written.
Spanish knowledge test: secondary sources say English and Spanish at most offices; not confirmed on azdot.gov.
Permit supervisor must hold a class A, B, C or D license, be at least 21, and sit beside the permittee (ARS 28-3154(B)(2)).
Minimum liability insurance 25/50/15 (ARS 28-4009, as amended for policies from July 1, 2020).
Under 21: any alcohol in the body while driving is illegal (ARS 4-244(34)). Extreme DUI 0.15 to under 0.20; 0.20 or more is a higher tier (ARS 28-1382).
Official Spanish manual exists as form 99-0137 (listed at https://azdot.gov/content/driver-lic-manualcustomer-service-guide-spanish); URL not verified.

Handbook checked 2026-10-09: Arizona Driver License Manual and Customer Service Guide, form 99-0117 R04/2022 (Revised February 2022), the owner-supplied PDF. Printed page = PDF page. Questions carry printed page numbers.

The manual does NOT state the knowledge test size, pass mark, retake wait, or test languages. 30 questions / 80% (24) and the next-business-day retake come from earlier azdot.gov notes and stay unconfirmed (az-009, az-010, az-011 remain medium). Test languages unknown; spanish and languages left null. Not English-only as far as known; the manual only says road-test directions are given in English (p. 8).

Manual: speeds when not posted 15 mph approaching a school crosswalk, 25 business/residential, 55 open highways or city freeways, 65 designated open highways, 75 rural freeways (p. 32). School crossing zone 15 mph, no passing (p. 34).
Manual: Move Over (p. 31) covers any vehicle with flashing lights pulled to the side, including private vehicles; move over one lane or slow down with caution.

Manual: 8+ points in 12 months = Traffic Survival School or suspension (p. 49); red light conviction = mandatory TSS (p. 30, 50); under-18 graduated driver: 1st conviction TSS, 2nd 3-month, 3rd 6-month suspension (p. 11-12).
Manual: school bus - stop in both directions except opposite direction on a roadway divided by a physical barrier; striping is not a divider (p. 31).
Manual: insurance minimum 25/50/15 (p. 8). Extreme DUI 0.15+, harsher at 0.20+ (p. 52).
